original_value: A synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system can be seriously contaminated by radio frequency systems because of working in the same microwave frequency bands, which would degrade the SAR image quality and affect the accuracy of image interpretation. In this paper, a novel radio frequency interference (RFI) suppression approach including RFI identification, band-stop filtering and a removed spectrum iterative adaptive approach (RSIAA) is proposed. First, the smoothing process is added before RFI signal detection to improve the RFI detection capacity. Afterwards, the band-stop filtering with a broaden factor is proposed to mitigate the residual RFI, and it ensures the accuracy of the following removed spectrum recovery by the RSIAA. Finally, the removed spectrum components are estimated from available adjacent spectrum data by the RSIAA in turn to obtain the desired range spectra. Compared with the conventional range frequency filtering method for RFI suppression, the capacity of the weak RFI signal detection is improved, and the increased sidelobes due to the discontinuous spectra are well suppressed. Simulation experiments on both simulated SAR raw data, Gaofen-3 and Sentinel-1 SAR raw data validate the proposed RFI suppression approach.

result.paraphrase: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems can suffer severe contamination from radio frequency systems since they operate in the same microwave frequency bands, degrading SAR image quality and reducing the accuracy of image interpretation. This paper proposes a new radio frequency interference (RFI) suppression method that combines RFI identification, band-stop filtering, and a removed spectrum iterative adaptive approach (RSIAA). First, smoothing is introduced before RFI signal detection to enhance detection capability. Next, band-stop filtering with an expanded factor is used to suppress residual RFI and to ensure accurate subsequent removed-spectrum recovery by RSIAA. Finally, RSIAA iteratively estimates the removed spectral components from the available adjacent spectrum data to recover the desired range spectra. Compared with conventional range-frequency filtering for RFI suppression, this method improves weak-RFI detection and effectively suppresses the increased sidelobes caused by discontinuous spectra. Simulation experiments using simulated SAR raw data as well as Gaofen-3 and Sentinel-1 SAR raw data confirm the effectiveness of the proposed RFI suppression approach.
